hypothesis: For translated-low small-dual plans and previously uncovered native-high full-public-loss plans, regular Algorithm 4/5 transforms are cheaper than compiling and executing ragged pruned schedules below the 1024-byte direct threshold.

shared_configuration.evidence_class: controlled directional; no external affinity-supervisor seal

scope: Translated-low production small-dual plans plus native-high maximum public loss only where the existing dense and one-coordinate boundary policies do not already skip schedules.
limitations: Candidate and control were sequential 11-repetition blocks without confidence intervals. Although the selector was logically inert in 48 existing-policy cells, changing the inline selector shifted hot-function text addresses; those controls therefore reveal a code-layout or timing-drift confound. Explicit LEGACY_HIGH R>K cells were not in this screen.
decision: Keep LEO2_EXPERIMENT_SMALL_DUAL_REGULAR_FALLBACK disabled by default. Isolate the selector from hot text layout or provide a same-binary diagnostic, then run committed-source ABBA with confidence intervals across affected and inert controls before reconsidering promotion.
conclusion: The affected region is promising, but the neighboring-control regressions fail the promotion gate and prevent a causal performance claim from this screen.
